series: JLPT N3 grammar series; denominator = 220 Bunpro N3 entries (n3-coverage-matrix, frozen)
levelPolicy: Bunpro precedence (docs/jlpt-levels.md); Rule A owning level kept for reused items; new items classified by the complete visible contrast; Rule B both Sensei and SKM at N3; Rule C N2 only where the exact sense is supported at N2 and N3 placement cannot be verified.

dispositions.levelEvidence: Bunpro N3 (entry listed); existing hope/wish practice kept at its N4 labels.
dispositions.note: Existing といい hope practice reused; two new interpretations add the advice ('should') sense: early-night with といい and hotel-route with ばいい (ばいい is owned by advice-certainty-denial and appears here only as protected context for the advice label, not as a target). Contrasted with permission readings (てもかまわない, てもいい). jlpt 3 because the contrast includes the N3 てもかまわない reading.
Contrast with the speaker's own て + みる (ids peephole-child, apple-grandchild), following Bunpro's caution that ごらん never describes one's own action.
Formation across godan, godan-exception and する verbs; past, potential-question and humble-announcement uses; contrast with plain てもらう (bike-repair, bakery-tip).

Permission, 'I don't mind' and negative なくてもかまわない; contrast with てはいけない (museum-photos, fast-river), with なければいけない in optional-practice and its pair team-selection (both options negative, so polarity alone does not decide), and with advice readings. manager-dayoff uses the near-synonym てもいい in an interpretation item.
Contrast with ないようにしている (evening-coffee, station-escalator).

About-to with an interruption (ようとしたら, leaving-phone), a non-volitional subject (closing-door) and an effort contradicted by the next sentence (baby-standing); contrast with てみる (natto-taste with みたら, app-handy with みたが), so the connective never predicts the answer.
Shares the attempt construction with row 151; the が-continuation states the failure or non-performance.
Includes する→せず; ないではいられない accepted as a typed variant; contrast with なければならない (weekly-report, daily-medicine).
Attachments Vない, な-adjective, Vている, Vた; contrast with ようだ (headphones-call, pale-colleague).

contrastSideLevels: All 47 new exercises are jlpt 3: every contrast-side target (てみる, ないようにしている, なければならない, てはいけない, てもらう, ようだ) is offered beside a well-formed N3 alternative in the same slot, so the complete visible task needs the N3 contrast (docs/jlpt-levels.md).

vocabulary.policy: Local displayed-form readings/glosses; no canonical word references; blank protected as grammar-target.

reviewLimits: No physical-device rendering check was performed.
Model-authored; independent model reviews recorded by the coordinator.

independentReview.method: Three blind single-facet reviews, each by a fresh agent with a different requested model family, given only the frozen render, raw set JSON, article and ledger: A linguistic correctness, B consistency and quiz safety, C learner comprehensibility. Findings were consolidated by the coordinator, applied by the author, and sent back to the original reviewers for a per-finding disposition.
independentReview.actualModelNote: The runtime does not expose the served model; the requested model is recorded.

reviews.finalVerdict: all findings resolved after reconciliation; no open high or medium findings

findings.claim: Only some spellings of ごらん／ご覧／御覧 (with or without なさい) were accepted.
findings.change: Accepted answers now systematically cover (kanji verb, kana verb) × (ごらん, ご覧, 御覧, ごらんなさい, ご覧なさい, 御覧なさい).

findings.claim: The rule 'よ addressed to a child calls for ごらん' was too mechanical.
findings.change: Rewritten: ごらん invites a junior listener to try; みる is the speaker's own trial, including a nonpast 'I'll try'.

findings.claim: Instructions asked for plain past (〜た) while ていた forms were accepted.
findings.change: Instructions now say 'plain past (〜た or 〜ていた)'; a scripted scan confirms no 〜た-only instruction accepts a ていた answer.

reviews.finalVerdict: all high and medium findings resolved after reconciliation; one low finding partly resolved by an accepted design choice

findings.claim: Typed mode hides the options, but instructions referred to 'the tense/aspect/politeness the options show'.
findings.change: Every typed instruction now names the required form, e.g. 'plain past (〜た)' or 'polite nonpast (〜ません)'.

findings.claim: The contexts did not clearly separate an attempt from a trial.
findings.change: leaving-phone uses an attempt-interrupted frame (出ようとしたら、電話が鳴って); app-handy uses てみたが + a disappointing result.

findings.location: noun-swap groups (teacher-name/locked-room/unsaid-words, natto-taste/app-handy, apple-grandchild, station-escalator, bakery-tip)
findings.claim: Several example keys were the same move with nouns swapped.
findings.change: Swapped items share one key or were given different connectives and frames (self-talk, dialogue answer, relative clause); every facet keeps at least 2 distinct keys.

findings.claim: About 20 article examples copied exercise items, revealing answers.
The distractor 思い出してみたが、思い出せなかった is arguably natural.
findings.change: Item removed; key attempt-failed stays covered by locked-room and unsaid-words; counts and ledger updated (48 → 47).

findings.claim: Ill-formed distractors (立ってみている, 閉まってみた) made items trivially easy.
findings.change: baby-standing redesigned (立とうとした vs 立ってみた, contradicted by the next sentence). closing-door keeps 閉まってみた as an intentional form-excluded item, recorded as a known doubt.
findings.disposition: partly resolved; remainder accepted by the coordinator

findings.claim: The distractor 来てはいけません mixed permission/prohibition into a no-need item.
findings.change: Distractor changed to 来なければいけません in a new no-need-or-must relationship; new item team-selection keys 来なければいけません.

findings.claim: The N3 frame was always listed first.
findings.change: One fixed option order per relationship, independent of the answer (answer first in 20/47).

findings.claim: All three used たらいい／てもかまわない, a repeated surface.
findings.change: Now ばいい (protected context), といい and てもいい respectively.

findings.claim: Stale exercise count in the ledger note.
